rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 mph zone with signs.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
